newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Farmers were being tight-lipped as of late last night about tactics for today's expected stand-off between themselves and police. Regional roads in Thessaly were the site of a game of cat and mouse between the riot police and squads of farmers overnight. Police are under orders to quickly dismantle possible blockades on national roads.

--Recent statements by Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos regarding the issue of the name for the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and his negative references to the Greece-FYROM interim accord were criticised by Prime Minister Costas Simitis at a meeting late last night of ruling party PASOK's Executive Bureau.

--The government is now facing the headache of an indefinite strike across the board in the education field. Meanwhile, there appears to be little hope of progress in demands put forward by civil servants, on the second day of a 48-hour strike.

--Reports from Moscow state that the Russian underworld used Athens as a base for activity in the rest of Europe, following the discovery of the body of hitman and former KGB agent Alexander Solonik in Athens. Last week the Russian authorities arrested a major underworld figure carrying an authentic Greek passport which named him as "Kolantopoulos".
--The police have effectively banned tractors from national roads in Thessaly but defiant farmers have said they will set up road blocks wherever the police stop them.

--High school teachers are on the verge of deciding to extend their strike for a fourth week, while it looks likely that primary school and kindergarten teachers will also continue their five-day strike.

--The government is facing a test of its policies on two fronts today. High school teachers are to decide today whether to extend their three-week strike and the fate of the farmers-police stand-off in Thessaly is expected to determine the course of farmers' protests in other regions around the country.
--Conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert clarified yesterday that he would be in the running for the post of party leader at the forthcoming congress. ETHNOS
--US President Clinton is expected to announce the US initiative on Cyprus and the Aegean in Washington today. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
